items.t: HRO: Loan Module Improvements – Bulk Loan Functionality
items.d: Selected. Try Lexi as the solution.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Two parts of the Loan module are not working as expected, and both affect how loans are closed off.

The first is the Bulk Loan Settlement page. NDB has around 2,800 employees, and in a single cycle around 100 loan settlements may need to be processed. The Bulk Loan Settlement page is meant for exactly this, but for NDB, it does not load. When a loan type is selected, the page loads every employee who holds that loan type, all ticked by default, before the user can choose who to settle. At this headcount that load is the likely point of failure. With the page unavailable, each settlement has to be made one employee at a time on the Loan Settlement screen, which means around 100 separate searches, selections and saves at the busiest point of the payroll cycle. A settlement that is missed or made late leaves an instalment to be deducted from a loan that should already be closed, and a settlement made for the wrong employee or loan cannot currently be reversed.

The second is the handling of loans when an employee resigns. Any loan still outstanding must be either settled, from the final settlement or by the employee, or made inactive so that payroll stops recovering it, depending on the case. This is not working as expected. The Inactivation option on the Loan Settlement screen and the Bulk Loan Settlement page halts a loan only for a set number of pay periods, which does not fit a leaver whose loan will never again be recovered through payroll. When a leaver's loan is not closed correctly, it stays active with an outstanding balance, appears in loan lists and reports as if it were still being recovered, and the amount owed is not dealt with in the employee's final settlement. If the employee is kept payroll-active for final settlement or arrears, an instalment can be deducted that should not be, or one that should be is missed.

Both issues push work back onto manual checks when there is least time for them. Payroll teams need the Bulk Loan Settlement page to work at the size of their largest clients, and need every leaver's loans settled or made inactive correctly and on time, with a record of what was done.

Solution Scope

Investigate and correct the existing Bulk Loan Settlement page and the settlement and inactivation of loans for resigned employees, so both work as intended for clients the size of NDB. This is a correction to delivered functionality: the Loan Settlement screen, the Bulk Loan Settlement page and the way payroll recovers and closes loans should be fixed and extended where needed, not replaced.

For Bulk Loan Settlement, the investigation should confirm why the page does not load at NDB's volume, starting with the load of every holder of the selected loan type, and change the page so it loads only the employees the user filters to, shows them in pages, and saves large batches without timing out.

For resigned employees, the reported failure should first be reproduced with NDB and the expected outcome agreed for each case. Early code reading of payroll loan recovery points to three areas to check first, none of them yet confirmed: an inactivation recorded for an employee for one month appears to stop recovery of all of that employee's loans in that calendar month, whatever the loan type and in any year; payroll closes a loan only when its balance reaches exactly zero, so a balance left over with no instalments remaining keeps the loan active indefinitely; and the final payment run appears to show loans on the final payslip without recovering them.

The corrections should work with related items. Loan Settlement Reversal extends the same Bulk Loan Settlement page, so bulk reversal should be built on the corrected page. The automatic payroll-inactive update for leavers in Payroll Input Validation & Readiness should flag leavers who still hold open loans before they are excluded. The Loan Details Summary already shown on the offboarding Exit Notice should be used to confirm that loans are closed before offboarding is finalised.

Solution List
  • Root-cause investigation of the Bulk Loan Settlement load failure using NDB-size data, recording load times at different numbers of loan holders before and after the fix
  • Bulk Loan Settlement page corrected to load at the volume of the largest clients, with filters such as company, pay group, employee and employee status applied before the loan list loads, and paging for long lists
  • Employees left unticked by default when the list loads, with a Select All option, so loans are settled only for the employees the user chooses
  • Option to load the employees and settlement amounts (Full or Part) from an Excel list, so around 100 settlements can be made in one step without picking each employee on screen
  • Background processing of large bulk settlements and inactivations, with a completion summary of the loans updated and those that failed, and the reason for each failure
  • Validation before saving, covering loans already settled, part settlement amounts above the balance, pending loan approvals and payroll period locks, with failed rows listed separately so valid rows can still be applied
  • Reproduction of the resigned employee loan issue with NDB, and the expected result agreed for each case: settled from the final settlement, settled by the employee, or made inactive
  • Loan inactivation corrected so that it applies only to the selected loan, for the selected pay periods of the correct year, and stops recovery of that loan only
  • Inactivation option for leavers that stops a loan from the resignation date onwards, rather than for a set number of pay periods
  • Loans closed correctly once nothing remains to be recovered, including a balance left over with no instalments remaining, so no loan stays active indefinitely
  • Outstanding loan balance shown and recoverable in the leaver's final payment where the loan type is set up for it, so the loan is settled with the final pay
  • Bulk Loan Settlement filter for resigned employees, so all leavers' loans for a period can be settled or inactivated in one step
  • Resigned Employees with Active Loans report per company and pay group, listing each leaver's resignation date, loan, balance and status
  • New Pre-Process Validation rule for employees whose resignation date falls in or before the payroll period and who still hold an active loan, configurable as Informational or Blocker
  • Open loan check in the automatic payroll-inactive update for leavers and at offboarding finalisation, so a leaver is not excluded from payroll or offboarded with a loan still open
  • History of individual and bulk settlements and inactivations, recording who acted, when, the loans affected and the values before and after
  • Regression testing of Loan Settlement, Bulk Loan Settlement, inactivation, payroll recovery, payroll rollback and final payment with NDB-size data before release

items.t: HRO: Provide a new option to rollback loan settlement.
items.d: Selected. Try Lexi as the solution.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Once a loan settlement is saved, it cannot be reversed. A full or part settlement entered on the Loan Settlement screen, or for a group of employees on the Bulk Loan Settlement page, reduces or clears the loan balance and outstanding instalments, records the settled amount and date on the loan schedule and, for a full settlement, marks the loan as settled. If the settlement was entered for the wrong employee, the wrong loan, the wrong amount or the wrong closure date, there is no way to undo it.

Settlement requests do change after they have been actioned. In HRO, a client may ask for a loan to be settled for Employee A and later tell HRO that the request was meant for Employee B. The settlement for Employee B can be processed, but Employee A's settlement stays in place. To correct it, a new loan has to be created for Employee A for the amount that was wrongly settled, and its instalments set up again by hand.

This workaround leaves two loan records where there should be one. The original loan shows as settled when it was not, and the replacement loan has a new reference, start date and schedule, so the loan history, interest and loan reports no longer match what actually happened. The original terms, such as interest rate, instalment amount and remaining instalments, must be re-entered and can easily differ from the original. Nothing links the replacement loan to the settlement it corrects or records why it was created, so the correction is hard to explain in an audit or when the employee or client queries the loan balance. If the replacement loan is not in place before the next payroll run, the instalment is not deducted that month and has to be recovered later.

As settlement requests change more often than the loan records allow, payroll and HRO teams need a controlled way to reverse a settlement made in error and return the loan to the state it was in before, with a clear record of who reversed it, when and why.

Solution Scope

Introduce a Loan Settlement Reversal capability that lets authorized users reverse a full or part settlement made in error. A reversal restores the original loan's balance, interest, outstanding instalments, schedule and active status to what they were before the settlement, under the same loan reference, and records the reversal against that loan. The correct settlement can then be applied to the right employee or loan.

The existing Loan Settlement screen and Bulk Loan Settlement page should be extended with the reversal rather than adding a separate screen, and the settlement details they already store, such as settled amount, settled date, closure date and comment, should drive the restore. The way payroll rollback already restores a loan's balance and active status should be assessed as a starting point. A reversal never creates a new loan. Settlements that have been followed by payroll runs, top-offs, re-schedules or inactivations need specific checks so the loan is not left in an inconsistent state.

Solution List
  • Reverse Settlement action on the Loan Settlement screen for full and part settlements, with settled loans available through Load Settled Loans
  • Restoration of the loan to its state before the settlement, covering balance amount, interest, total and balance instalments, schedule rows (settled amount, settled date, last settled number and process status) and active and settled status, under the original loan reference and terms
  • Reverse and re-apply option that reverses a settlement and applies the same amount, closure date and comment to the correct employee or loan in one step, for cases such as a request made for the wrong employee
  • Reversal of settlements made through Bulk Loan Settlement, for selected employees or for the whole batch
  • Reversal of part settlements in order, latest first, so that where a loan has several settlements the schedule is unwound correctly
  • Checks before reversal for later changes to the loan, such as a top-off, re-schedule or inactivation made after the settlement, with the reversal blocked or the later change listed for the user to reverse first
  • Handling of instalments that fell due between the settlement and its reversal, listing instalments not deducted in payroll runs processed in between, with the option to recover them in the next payroll run or spread them over the remaining instalments
  • Payroll period lock checks that flag a reversal affecting a processed or locked payroll period and stop it from changing that period's processed results
  • Configurable limit on how far back a settlement can be reversed, such as within the current payroll period or a set number of days after the closure date
  • Mandatory reversal reason from a configurable list, such as wrong employee, wrong loan, wrong amount or request withdrawn by the client, with a comment and an attachment for the client's instruction
  • Role-based permission to reverse settlements, separate from the permission to settle, with an optional approval workflow before the reversal is applied
  • Loan history and schedule showing the settlement and its reversal as linked entries, with the restored balance
  • Configurable notification to the loan administrator and the employee when a settlement is reversed, showing the restored balance and next instalment
  • Loan Settlement Reversal report per company and period, listing each reversed settlement with the employee, loan, amount, reason, and who reversed and approved it
  • Audit trail recording who reversed which settlement, when and why, with the loan values before and after the reversal

items.t: HRO P1: EIM Field Modification via Data Import - Existing Employees / New Employees
items.d: Selected. Try Lexi as the solution.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

HRO manages employee data for clients with large headcounts. Most changes are made through the front end by searching for each employee and updating the record one at a time. Month-end and increment cycles bring these changes in volume, for example:

  • resignation dates for around 150 employees in one month
  • new designations for 500 to 600 employees during an increment cycle

Each change is a separate search, edit and save.

The changes fall into two groups:

  • Fields without dependencies can be updated without affecting anything else: Cost Center, Resignation Date, Retirement Date, the HR, Payroll and Attendance flags, Address and TIN Number. Bank details also need to be added for new joiners and changed for existing employees.
  • Fields with dependencies are Designation and Department. A change to either is a movement in the employee’s career. It must be recorded with an effective date and history, and it can bring related changes and rules with it. These fields cannot simply be overwritten in bulk without the checks the individual screens apply.

Master data has the same problem. There is no bulk upload for EIM definitions, so entries such as cost centres and designations are added one at a time. A single client can need 10 new cost centres and 50 new designations, and clients such as IFS or IGT use a large number of different designations. Employee uploads must not create master data automatically, so these definitions have to exist before employee data is loaded. Slow master data entry therefore also holds up employee updates and new joiner imports.

Imports for new employees need one more check. Before loading, HRO must confirm that these required fields are available and use the expected field names:

  • Wages Board
  • Shop/Office
  • Statutory Classification
  • Employment Category
  • Employee Group

HRO finds missing or differently named fields by eye and corrects them by hand. A missed field is only noticed after the employees have been created.

Doing all of this one record at a time takes days of HRO effort at the busiest point of the month. It increases the chance of keying errors and missed records, and it leaves no single record of what was changed in a batch.

As client headcounts grow, HRO needs to do three things in bulk: update many employees from a single file, add master data definitions, and confirm that new employee files carry the required fields before import. Dependent fields must keep their effective dates, history and rules.

Solution Scope

Introduce a Bulk Employee & Master Data Upload capability that lets HRO:

  • update selected fields for many employees from one Excel file
  • add EIM master data definitions such as cost centres and designations in bulk
  • confirm that required fields are present and correctly named before a new employee import

Every row is checked before anything is saved. Dependent changes such as Designation and Department go through the proper movement rules instead of being overwritten directly.

This should build on what already exists:

  • EIM Excel upload: The existing Data Sheet Upload / View already supports areas such as Bulk Employee Details and Employee Assignment Details. It should be extended with these fields and with master data definitions, rather than adding separate uploaders.
  • ELC movements: Designation and Department changes should go through the existing Employee Lifecycle (ELC) movement process, with effective date, approval and history. A bulk change then leaves the same record as an individual one.
  • Master data control: The bulk definition upload is the controlled way to add master data. Employee uploads still never create it. Values they flag as missing can be added through the definition upload, and the affected rows run again.
  • The other two theses: Client files can be brought into these templates through Client File Mapping & Import. Bulk resignation date updates should feed the automatic payroll-inactive update in Payroll Input Validation & Readiness.
Solution List
  • Field-selectable bulk update template: HRO chooses the fields to update and downloads a template with only those columns, pre-filled with employee numbers and current values for the selected employees
  • Bulk update of fields without dependencies: Cost Center, Resignation Date, Retirement Date, HR, Payroll and Attendance flags, Address and TIN Number
  • Bulk add and update of bank details for new joiners and existing employees, with checks on bank, branch and account number format
  • Bulk Designation and Department changes processed as ELC movements with effective date, reason and history, applying the same dependency rules as the individual screens
  • Option to send bulk Designation and Department changes for approval as one batch, or apply them directly, based on the user’s role and configuration
  • Required field check for new employee imports: before any rows are processed, confirm that Wages Board, Shop/Office, Statutory Classification, Employment Category and Employee Group are present and set up for the client under the expected names, with differently named fields matched through the client’s saved mapping
  • Bulk upload of EIM master data definitions, starting with cost centres and designations and extendable to other definitions such as departments, employment categories and employee groups, with a downloadable template for each definition type
  • Duplicate checks on new definitions, including names that differ only in case, spacing or punctuation, so the same cost centre or designation is not added twice
  • Missing master data flagged during an employee import collected into a definition upload file, so HRO can review and add the definitions in one step and then run the affected employee rows again
  • Row-level checks before saving:
  • the employee exists
  • values match existing master data such as cost centres, designations, departments and banks
  • dates make sense, such as resignation after joining
  • there are no duplicate rows
  • no master data is created through employee uploads
  • Blank cells treated as “no change”, so only the values entered in the file are updated
  • Preview of current and new values for every row before submission, with invalid rows listed separately with reasons and a downloadable error file
  • Partial processing: valid rows are applied, and failed rows can be fixed and uploaded again
  • Batch history recording who uploaded which file, the employees and definitions affected, the fields changed, and the old and new values

items.t: HRO P1: Data Import Tool Data Auto Populate
items.d: Selected. Try Lexi as the solution.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

During every monthly payroll cycle, the HRO team receives payroll data from each client as Excel files. Every client sends its own layout, with different column names, column order and value formats, and the layout can change from one month to the next.

These files cannot be uploaded directly. If a client file contains a hierarchy, pay group or designation that does not already exist in the system, the upload may create it automatically. A misspelt or differently named value therefore adds unwanted master data and can place employees under the wrong structure. This causes problems in payroll processing and reporting that must be cleaned up afterwards. Employee codes are a second problem. The system requires a six-digit employee code, but clients often send codes without leading zeros, such as 18 instead of 000018, so rows do not match the correct employee.

To work around this, HRO staff manually map or re-key each client file into a dedicated standard template before uploading it. They repeat this for every client every month, at the busiest point of the payroll cycle. The work relies on individual knowledge of each client’s format, and it allows mapping and copy errors that are often found only after upload or after the pay run.

As the HRO client base grows, the team needs to take each client’s file in its own format, map it once, check it against existing master data, and upload it. This should happen without manual re-keying and without master data being created by accident.

Solution Scope

Introduce a Client File Mapping & Import capability that does three things:

  • It converts a client’s Excel file into the standard upload format, using a saved mapping for that client.
  • It validates every row against existing master data before anything is written.
  • It passes only clean data to the existing uploads.

The import should send its output to what HRO already uses, not replace it. That means the existing upload screens (such as Upload Bulk Pay Items and the employee upload) and the standard template HRO uses today, including the one that feeds the Payroll RPA process. The existing pay item Upload Configuration already maps data source columns to pay item fields, so it should be assessed as a starting point for the mapping. Hierarchies, pay groups and designations must never be created through this import. Values that do not match an existing record are held for the user to map or correct.

Solution List
  • Client mapping profiles that save each client’s column-to-field mapping once and reuse it every payroll cycle, with a new version when the client changes its file layout
  • Upload of client Excel files in their original format, with the client’s saved mapping applied automatically and a preview of the mapped data before submission
  • Value mapping of client names and codes for hierarchies, pay groups, designations and other reference data to existing system records, remembered for future cycles
  • Pre-upload validation against existing master data, with no automatic creation of hierarchies, pay groups or designations, and unmatched values flagged for correction
  • Employee code normalization that adds leading zeros up to the required length (six digits) and confirms each code matches an existing employee
  • Standardization of dates, amounts and text values (number formats, extra spaces, blank cells) to the format the upload expects
  • Validation summary with a downloadable error file listing each rejected row and its reason, so only failed rows need to be fixed and re-uploaded
  • Hand-off of validated data to the existing employee and pay item uploads, and output in the standard template used by the Payroll RPA process
  • Import history per client and pay period, recording the file uploaded, the mapping version used, who ran it, and the result

items.t: HRO P1: Payroll Field Modification via Data Import
items.d: Selected. Try Lexi as the solution.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

When HRO sets up a batch of new employees, often around 100 at a time, each employee also needs a payroll profile. There is no bulk upload for payroll profiles. HRO completes them one employee at a time on the Add Employees to Payroll screen. Each profile includes:

  • the applicable tax flags, such as APIT Lump Sum and SD Terminal Tax (One-time Payment Tax)
  • the Employee Pay Mode (Cash or Bank)

For each employee, HRO opens the profile, ticks the correct tax flags, sets the pay mode and saves. For 100 employees, that is the same set of clicks repeated 100 times, at the busiest point of the payroll cycle.

Mistakes are easy to make and hard to see:

  • A missed tax flag only shows up when tax on a lump-sum or terminal payment is calculated wrongly.
  • A wrong pay mode only shows up when an employee meant to be paid by bank is paid in cash, or the other way round.

Both have to be corrected after the payroll run.

As client headcounts grow, HRO needs to set up payroll profiles for new and existing employees in bulk from a single file. The upload should apply the same checks as the individual screen.

Solution Scope

Introduce a Bulk Employee Payroll Profile Upload that lets HRO set payroll profile fields, including tax flags and pay mode, for many employees from one Excel file. Every row is checked before anything is saved.

This should build on what already exists:

  • Add Employees to Payroll: The upload should follow the existing screen and its Employee Payroll Details rules, so a profile created in bulk matches one created on screen.
  • Client tax setup: The tax flag columns should come from the taxes set up for each client, so the template matches that client’s configuration.
  • Bulk Employee & Master Data Upload: This upload is the payroll counterpart to that thesis. It should share the same template, checks, preview, error file and history approach. Employees set to Bank pay mode should be checked against the bank details captured there.
  • Payroll RPA: A native bulk upload gives the RPA process a direct route for this step, instead of filling in the screen one employee at a time.
Solution List
  • Bulk payroll profile template for new and existing employees, pre-filled with employee numbers for the selected employees or for those not yet added to payroll
  • New employees added to payroll and their profile completed in the same upload, instead of a separate step per employee
  • Bulk setting of tax flags, such as APIT Lump Sum and SD Terminal Tax (One-time Payment Tax), with the columns generated from the taxes set up for the client
  • Bulk setting of Employee Pay Mode (Cash or Bank), with a check that every employee on Bank pay mode has active bank details
  • Coverage of the other Employee Payroll Details fields, such as salary grade, schema, native currency, next increment date, payroll active status and Additional Fields, so a full profile can be set in one upload
  • Blank cells filled with pay group defaults, such as the standard pay mode and tax flags, for new employees, and treated as “no change” for existing employees
  • Row-level checks before saving:
  • the employee exists and is HR active
  • the tax flags are valid for the employee’s pay group
  • values match existing master data such as salary grades, schemas and currencies
  • no master data is created through the upload
  • Preview of current and new values for every row before submission, with invalid rows listed separately with reasons and a downloadable error file
  • Partial processing: valid rows are applied, and failed rows can be fixed and uploaded again
  • Batch history recording who uploaded which file, the employees affected, and the old and new values, including every tax flag and pay mode change
  • New Pre-Process Validation rules for payroll employees with no tax flags, no pay mode, or Bank pay mode without bank details, so incomplete profiles are caught before the payroll run

items.t: Implementability - Script Debugging and Editing Tool for Implementation Teams

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Implementation teams currently need direct database access, or help from the backend team, to debug, edit and run dynamic scripts during client implementations and support. Issues wait on backend availability, fixes take longer to reach clients, and script changes are made without consistent validation, testing or a reliable record of what was changed.

Direct database access for implementation teams is also a security and compliance risk. Scripts can be changed or run outside any access control, there is no dependable before-and-after history, and a faulty change is hard to trace or reverse.

Solution Scope

Deliver a secure Dynamic Script Management tool where authorised implementation users can debug, edit and run dynamic scripts without direct database access or backend team involvement.

The tool gives implementation teams one controlled place to see a script's parameters, results and errors, make validated changes, and test them with a preview run before they are applied. Role-based access, a full audit trail and version history make every edit and run accountable and reversible. Once the tool is in place, direct database access will be removed from implementation teams. This will speed up issue resolution, reduce dependency on the backend team, and improve security and compliance.

Solution List
  • Script Explorer — Find and View Dynamic Scripts
  • Script Debugging — Parameters, Results and Error Details
  • In-Tool Script Editor with Validation Before Save
  • Test / Preview Run Before Changes Are Applied
  • Controlled Script Execution
  • Role-Based Access — View, Edit and Run Permissions
  • Audit Trail of Edits and Runs — Who, What, When, and Before and After Versions
  • Version History, Comparison and Rollback
  • Removal of Direct Database Access for Implementation Teams

items.t: Implementability - Automated Attendance Comparison Tool for Payroll Parallel Runs

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

During a payroll parallel run, implementation teams check PeoplesHR attendance results against the parallel-run baseline by hand, usually by exporting data and comparing spreadsheets employee by employee and day by day. This is slow, depends on individual effort, and is easy to get wrong. Issues such as missing punches, incorrectly applied leave and overtime mismatches can be missed or found late.

Issues found late lead to extra parallel-run cycles, delayed go-lives and payroll corrections after go-live. As implementations grow in size and complexity, implementation teams need a structured, repeatable and auditable way to confirm attendance is correct for each payroll period before final payroll processing.

Solution Scope

Introduce an Attendance Parallel Run Validation capability for payroll parallel runs.

For a selected payroll period and employee group, the solution will automatically compare PeoplesHR attendance results with the parallel-run baseline and flag every difference as an exception. Exceptions will be reported by employee, date and issue type, with export. Implementation teams can correct the issues and re-run the comparison until attendance is accurate, before payroll is finalised. The comparison should use the attendance results PeoplesHR already produces, not a separate recalculation of attendance.

Solution List
  • Parallel-Run Baseline Import: template upload and field mapping
  • Comparison Run Setup: payroll period and employee group selection
  • Attendance Comparison Engine: employee-by-date comparison of PeoplesHR results against the baseline
  • Exception Detection: missing punches, incorrect leave, OT mismatches, shift and roster differences, absence and attendance status mismatches, and other differences
  • Configurable Comparison Rules and Tolerances, such as an acceptable OT minute variance
  • Exception Classification by Issue Type and Severity
  • Exception Report by employee, date and issue type, with filters and export
  • Comparison Summary: match rate, exceptions by type and employees affected
  • Exception Drill-Down to the source punches, leave and roster data
  • Exception Status Tracking: Open, Corrected, and Accepted as Valid Difference with a reason
  • Re-run Comparison after corrections, showing resolved, new and remaining exceptions
  • Comparison Run History and Audit Trail
  • Attendance Readiness Sign-Off before final payroll processing

items.t: Implementability - Error Handling Framework Rollout to Remaining Modules
items.d: Earlier this has been handled through techdebts.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

The error handling framework is implemented in only some modules. The remaining modules log errors in different ways, so the same type of failure can produce very different log output depending on where it happens. Implementation and support teams then spend extra time collecting information, reproducing issues and tracing the root cause. This slows down issue resolution and adds to technical debt.

The problem is harder for clients who do not allow their systems to connect to the internet. For these offline or on-premise clients, error information cannot be collected remotely. Support teams depend on manual log collection and back-and-forth with the client's IT team.

As more clients go live, implementation and support teams need error logs that are consistent across every module and can be accessed for every deployment model.

Solution Scope

Complete the rollout of the existing Error Handling Framework across all modules.

The work starts with a gap assessment to identify the modules not yet covered. Those modules are then prioritised by support ticket volume, customer impact and usage, and a rollout plan is agreed. The framework is implemented in the prioritised modules by following the existing implementation, so every module produces the same error logs. The work also defines and implements an approach for offline and on-premise clients, such as local log storage with export.

The existing framework should be reused as the standard rather than redesigned. The expected outcome is consistent error logs across all modules, faster root cause analysis and reduced technical debt.

Solution List
  • Module Gap Assessment: modules where the framework is not yet implemented
  • Module Prioritisation: support ticket volume, customer impact and usage
  • Agreed Rollout Plan and sequencing
  • Framework Implementation in prioritised modules, following the existing implementation
  • Consistent Error Log output across all modules
  • Offline / On-Premise Logging Approach
  • Local Log Storage for clients without internet connectivity
  • Log Export for implementation and support teams

items.t: Disciplinary Module - PH specific Improvement Scoping

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Philippine law tells an employer how to discipline, not what to discipline for. Before a dismissal for just cause the employer must serve a Notice to Explain that names the rule broken and narrates the facts, give the employee at least five calendar days from receipt to answer, hold a hearing when one is requested or the facts are disputed, and serve a written decision. Each notice needs proof that the employee received it. Preventive suspension cannot run past 30 days unpaid. If the case reaches a labour tribunal, the burden of proving both the ground and the procedure rests on the employer (Labor Code Art. 292(b)).

PeoplesHR's Disciplinary module records what happened: the incident, witnesses, evidence, panel and corrective action. It does not run what the employer must do next, or when. There are no notices, no response clocks, no hearing record, no decision notice and no proof of service. The legally significant part of the process therefore happens outside the system, and the evidence an employer needs to defend itself ends up scattered across documents, inboxes and paper files.

Solution Scope

Turn the Disciplinary module from an incident register into a configurable due process capability in base code, so an employer can take a case from incident to decision inside PeoplesHR, with every notice, deadline and proof of service recorded, and export one case file that carries its burden of proof. The law lives in a country configuration pack, not in code, and the Philippines ships first. Phase 1 delivers the minimum lawful case: a configurable code of discipline, notices with proof of service, the response clock, decision support and the case file. Phase 2 completes the process with the hearing step, progressive discipline, preventive suspension and the handoffs to Offboarding and Payroll. Authorised cause terminations, employee grievances, AI drafting and litigation tracking are out of scope. This scope is provisional until the build state check and PH counsel review in section 8 are done.

Answers the problem in [[disciplinary-ph-business-problem]]. Traces to the improvement items in [[disciplinary-ph-gap-analysis]] section 8.

1. Scope principles
  1. Extend, do not replace. The incident register, witnesses and evidence, panel assignment, per employee actions, appeal, ESS view and incident history stay as they are. The new capability wraps around them.
  2. Configure, do not customise. The process engine is country neutral and lives in base code. Country rules (minimum response days, hearing triggers, grounds, templates, caps) live in a configuration pack. A new market is a new pack, not a change request.
  3. Record evidence, not only events. Every stage produces something the employer can show a tribunal: a notice, a proof of service, an explanation or a recorded non response, minutes, a decision with reasons.
  4. Guide by default, stop only at legal floors. Three hard stops, listed below. Everything else is a warning that can be overridden with a recorded justification, because the employer owns the decision.
  5. Existing customers see no change until they opt in. The current four corrective actions are seeded into the new configurable list, and existing incidents keep working.

The three hard stops

Hard stop

Rule it enforces

A response deadline cannot be set earlier than the country minimum, counted from the receipt date

PH: at least 5 calendar days from receipt (DO 147-15 Sec 5.1(a))

A decision cannot be issued before the response deadline unless the employee's explanation is on record

Ample opportunity to be heard (Art. 292(b) [277(b)])

An unpaid preventive suspension cannot run past the country cap

PH: 30 days, then reinstate or pay (Omnibus Rules Book V)

items.t: PH - Philhealth Changes: Solo Parent Employee Contribution Waved off

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

PhilHealth Circular 2026-0015, signed on 23 September 2026 under the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act (RA 11861), makes registered solo parents and their qualifying dependents automatically covered by PhilHealth, with the National Government paying their premiums. For employed solo parents, the National Government now pays the 2.5% employee share, and the employer continues to pay its 2.5% share. The total 5% premium and how it is calculated stay the same. The change applies to payroll from October 2026.

Philippine payroll currently deducts the PhilHealth employee share from every employee. Once PhilHealth tags an employee as a solo parent, it bills the employer for the employer share only. If payroll does not match PhilHealth's tagging exactly, one of two things goes wrong:

  • If payroll keeps deducting after the employee is tagged, the employee is over-deducted and the employer must refund them.
  • If payroll stops deducting before the employee is tagged, the employer ends up paying the employee's share.

To qualify, the employee needs a valid Solo Parent ID (SPIC) from their local government. The SPIC must be renewed every year, so an employee's status can change from one month to the next. Employers must also certify their solo parent employees to PhilHealth, track each employee's SPIC renewal, and keep evidence for that certification, because falsified IDs and false declarations carry administrative, civil and criminal liability.

Today there is no way to record solo parent status or to stop the employee share for individual employees. HR and payroll teams have to track eligibility, adjust deductions and keep evidence by hand every payroll.

Solution Scope

Extend the existing Philippines payroll PhilHealth contribution processing to support the Solo Parent Premium Subsidy under PhilHealth Circular 2026-0015.

HR will be able to record and maintain each employee's solo parent status, SPIC details and PhilHealth tagging. Payroll will check eligibility every month and stop the employee PhilHealth share only for months in which the employee has a valid SPIC and is tagged by PhilHealth. The employer share continues unchanged. When an SPIC expires, the employee automatically returns to the standard contribution.

The solution will also support certification to PhilHealth, SPIC renewal tracking, correction of mismatched months, and an auditable record of evidence and status changes. The existing PhilHealth calculation should be reused and extended wherever possible rather than creating a separate contribution type.

Solution List
  • Solo Parent details on the Employee Profile: SPIC number, issuing LGU, issue and expiry dates
  • SPIC document upload and evidence retention
  • Employee self-service submission of SPIC and renewals, with HR verification
  • PhilHealth solo parent tagging status and effective month
  • Employer certification list of solo parent employees for PhilHealth
  • Monthly payroll eligibility check (valid SPIC and PhilHealth tag)
  • Employee PhilHealth share exemption, with the employer share unchanged
  • Automatic return to the standard contribution when an SPIC expires
  • SPIC expiry warnings and renewal notifications to HR and employees
  • Refund adjustments for over-deducted employee share
  • Reconciliation of payroll treatment against PhilHealth billing
  • Payslip and PhilHealth contribution report updates showing the government-paid employee share
  • Audit trail of solo parent status, tagging and eligibility changes
  • Solo parent reports: tagged and untagged employees, upcoming expiries, exemptions applied

items.t: AI Insights - Dynamic Multi-Chart Insight Generation

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Analytical questions often cannot be fully understood through a single chart or visualization. Users may need to see multiple perspectives—such as overall KPIs, trends, comparisons, detailed records, and contextual explanations—to properly understand a business situation and make informed decisions.

When an analytical response is limited to one visual output, users may need to ask several follow-up questions to build the complete picture. This makes the analysis process more fragmented and reduces the value users can obtain from a single interaction.

Solution Scope

Enhance AI Insights to dynamically generate multiple relevant analytical outputs within a single response based on the user’s question, available data, and analytical context.

Instead of being restricted to a single chart, AI Insights should determine the most appropriate combination of visualizations and supporting insights required to answer the question effectively.

The generated response may include charts, KPI cards, tables, summaries, and recommendations where relevant. The number and type of outputs should be determined dynamically rather than being fixed for every query.

This is primarily a product enhancement intended to improve the overall AI Insights experience and is not currently driven by a confirmed customer requirement or sales blocker.

Concise List of Items
  • Dynamic generation of multiple analytical outputs
  • Multiple charts within a single AI Insights response
  • KPI cards where relevant
  • Supporting tables and detailed data views
  • AI-generated summaries and key observations
  • Recommendations where applicable
  • Automatic selection of suitable visualization types
  • Output combination based on question context and available data
  • Avoid unnecessary or repetitive visualizations
  • Maintain a clear and usable response layout

items.t: Mobile ChatBot - Manual In/Out Submission

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employees may need to submit Manual In or Manual Out requests as part of their regular attendance self-service process. This can include missed attendance events, attendance adjustments, or situations where a manual attendance entry is required based on company processes.

When this capability is not available through the Mobile Chatbot, employees must leave the conversational experience and navigate through separate application screens to complete the request. This creates a fragmented self-service experience and reduces the practical value of the chatbot for common attendance-related activities.

Solution Scope

Extend the Mobile Chatbot to support Manual In/Out application and submission, allowing employees to complete the process conversationally from within the chatbot.

The chatbot should collect the required information, such as applicable date, In/Out time, and reason, and submit the request through the existing Manual In/Out process.

The capability should follow the same validations, approval workflows, permissions, configurations, and company attendance policies already available in PeoplesHR.

Although the requirement is currently driven by one customer, Manual In/Out is a common attendance self-service requirement and can expand the Mobile Chatbot's usefulness for broader attendance-related activities.

Concise List of Items
  • Apply for Manual In through Mobile Chatbot
  • Apply for Manual Out through Mobile Chatbot
  • Capture applicable date and time
  • Capture reason/comment where required
  • Validate required information before submission
  • Follow existing Manual In/Out business rules
  • Follow existing approval workflows
  • Respect company attendance policies and configurations
  • Respect employee eligibility and permissions
  • Provide submission confirmation
  • Provide applicable validation and error messages
  • Reuse the existing Manual In/Out process and backend logic where applicable

items.t: Mobile - Team Prior OT Application

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employees and supervisors may need to submit Prior OT applications as part of overtime planning and attendance management.

When these activities depend on the web application, mobile-first employees and supervisors may not be able to submit Prior OT requests conveniently at the point of need. This can delay overtime planning and create unnecessary dependency on desktop access or HR support.

Solution Scope

Introduce Prior OT Application capabilities in the PeoplesHR mobile application, allowing users to submit Prior OT requests for themselves and, where authorized, supervisors to submit Prior OT requests for their team members.

The mobile experience should follow the existing Prior OT rules, validations, approval workflows, company configurations, employee eligibility, and supervisor access permissions already available in PeoplesHR.

This remains a lower-priority mobile enablement item, as Prior OT is not applicable to every organization and has comparatively lower customer and operational impact than broader mobile-first capabilities.

Concise List of Items
  • Self Prior OT Application
  • Team Prior OT Application
  • Select applicable subordinate/team member where authorized
  • Submit Prior OT for self
  • Submit Prior OT on behalf of a team member
  • Capture required OT date, time, duration, and applicable details
  • Follow existing Prior OT business rules and validations
  • Follow existing approval workflows
  • Respect employee and supervisor permissions
  • Follow company-level OT configurations and policies
  • Show applicable confirmation and validation messages
  • Maintain consistency with the existing web Prior OT process

items.t: Mobile ChatBot - Enable Attachment Handling for Leave Applications

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employees may need to provide supporting documents when applying for certain types of leave, such as medical certificates, official letters, or other evidence required by company policy.

When the Mobile Chatbot supports leave application but cannot handle mandatory attachments, employees are unable to complete those leave requests through the chatbot end-to-end. They must switch to another application flow, which creates a fragmented experience and reduces the effectiveness of chatbot-based self-service.

Solution Scope

Enhance the Mobile Chatbot Leave Application flow to support attachment handling, allowing employees to upload required supporting documents directly during the chatbot-based leave application process.

The chatbot should recognize when an attachment is required based on the selected leave type and existing leave configurations, allow the employee to upload the relevant document, and continue the application through the existing leave submission process.

The capability should follow the same attachment rules, validations, permissions, and leave policies already configured in PeoplesHR.

Although the request is currently driven by one customer, mandatory document submission is a common leave-management requirement and will make the Mobile Chatbot leave application flow more complete.

Concise List of Items
  • Upload attachments during chatbot leave application
  • Support mandatory attachments based on leave type
  • Support optional attachments where applicable
  • Detect attachment requirements from existing leave configuration
  • Allow supported document/file types
  • Apply existing file size and attachment validations
  • Show validation when a mandatory attachment is missing
  • Attach uploaded documents to the relevant leave request
  • Follow existing leave rules, eligibility, and approval workflows
  • Respect existing permissions and company configurations
  • Provide upload success/failure feedback
  • Allow users to complete applicable leave applications end-to-end through the Mobile Chatbot
